  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2"],
  "headline": "Intake established the browser game outcome, implementation boundaries, and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Deliver a small Battleship game playable by one person in a browser against a computer opponent. [assumption]: The entry point is a locally served browser page; the named browser target authorizes delivery there, while no deployed destination is specified. [assumption]: One browser session represents the player without sign-in; game state is private to that session, is not shared across people or devices, and ends when the session is closed or a new game starts. This default rules out accounts, multiplayer, cross-device continuity, and persistent saves. [open question, discovery]: Establish what the runtime provides for session identity and state before selecting a state mechanism; this blocks that selection. [open question, discovery]: Establish any existing rules or interface conventions before choosing details such as ship placement and computer moves; absent evidence, record conventional Battleship rules as the default. This blocks finalizing those details. [risk]: Rules and computer behavior must be understandable enough for a player to complete a game. S2 [fact]: Use Node.js for the server and include tests. [open question, discovery]: Establish available Node.js tooling and test conventions before choosing the server and test setup; absent evidence, record a minimal setup as the default. This blocks that tooling choice. [boundary, fact]: The repository is empty and this unattended intake stage implements nothing; discovery has no named team, workspace channel, internal site, document, private repository, owner, or ambiguous term to use as a source hint. [boundary, fact]: A person-only decision remains open, but work is blocked only if nothing can proceed without it. [visibility, fact]: The game becomes usable in the browser when a later implementation is run; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and a deployed outcome exists only after release."
}
